'''Tina van de Flierdt''' (born 1973) is a Professor of [[Isotope geochemistry|Isotope Geochemistry]] at [[Imperial College London]].

== Education ==
Van de Flierdt grew up in rural western Germany.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://forecastpod.org/index.php/2016/05/16/paleoceanography-proxies/|title=Tina van de Flierdt explains paleoceanography proxies|date=2016-05-16|work=Forecast: a podcast about climate science and climate scientists|access-date=2018-03-17|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2000 van de Flierdt completed a diploma in Geology at the [[University of Bonn]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/tina-van-de-flierdt-10766/|title=Tina van de Flierdt|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref> She earned a PhD at [[ETH Zurich]] in 2003, working with [[Alexander Halliday]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=de|first=Flierdt, Tina van|title=The Nd, Hf, and Pb isotopic composition of ferromanganese crusts and their paleoceanographic implications|date=2003|publisher=ETH Zurich|url=https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/147790|doi=10.3929/ethz-a-004630463|hdl=20.500.11850/147790 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Van de Flierdt is interested in the marine-terminating sector of the [[East Antarctic Ice Sheet]] during past warm periods.<ref name=":0" /> Her research looks to develop new geochemical and isotopic tracers in marine geochemistry, paleoceanography and paleoclimate, with particular focus on radiogenic isotopes.<ref name="Flierdt 20150293">{{Cite journal|last1=Flierdt|first1=Tina van de|last2=Griffiths|first2=Alexander M.|last3=Lambelet|first3=Myriam|last4=Little|first4=Susan H.|last5=Stichel|first5=Torben|last6=Wilson|first6=David J.|date=2016-11-28|title=Neodymium in the oceans: a global database, a regional comparison and implications for palaeoceanographic research|journal=Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A|language=en|volume=374|issue=2081|article-number=20150293|doi=10.1098/rsta.2015.0293|issn=1364-503X|pmid=29035258|pmc=5069528|bibcode=2016RSPTA.37450293V}}</ref> She is co-lead of the MAGIC Isotope group in the Department of Earth Sciences at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/earth-science/research/research-groups/magic/people/|title=People {{!}} Faculty of Engineering {{!}} Imperial College London|website=www.imperial.ac.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She is also a research at the [[Lamont–Doherty Earth Observatory]] at [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/user/tina|title=tina {{!}} Lamont–Doherty Earth Observatory|website=www.ldeo.columbia.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.earth.columbia.edu/eidirectory/view/1598|title=Dr. Tina Van De Flierdt – Directory – The Earth Institute – Columbia University|website=www.earth.columbia.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref>

She is part of the international [[Geotraces]] program.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ukgeotraces.com/participants/profiles/imperial/van_de_flierdt|title=van de Flierdt – UK Geotraces|website=www.ukgeotraces.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref> Part of the Geotraces program is to ensure results for trace elements and isotopes collected on different cruises by different laboratories can be compared in a meaningful way.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van de Flierdt|first1=Tina|last2=Pahnke|first2=Katharina|last3=Amakawa|first3=Hiroshi|last4=Andersson|first4=Per|last5=Basak|first5=Chandranath|last6=Coles|first6=Barry|last7=Colin|first7=Christophe|last8=Crocket|first8=Kirsty|last9=Frank|first9=Martin|date=2012|title=GEOTRACES intercalibration of neodymium isotopes and rare earth element concentrations in seawater and suspended particles. Part 1: reproducibility of results for the international intercomparison|url=https://eprints.esc.cam.ac.uk/2553/|journal=Limnology and Oceanography: Methods|language=en|volume=10|issue=4|pages=234–251|doi=10.4319/lom.2012.10.234|s2cid=129435466 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Van de Flierdt is building a global database of neodymium in the oceans and researching the implications for [[paleoceanography]] research.<ref name="Flierdt 20150293"/>

In 2012, she won a [[Leverhulme Trust]] grant to research deep sea corals.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/fr/news/grant-winners/419014.article|title=Grant winners|date=2012-02-16|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=2018-03-17|language=fr}}</ref> She was part of the [[Natural Environment Research Council]] project SWEET, ''Super-Warm Early Eocene Temperatures and climate''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/projects?ref=NE%2FP019080%2F1|title=SWEET:Super-Warm Early Eocene Temperatures and climate: understanding the response of the Earth to high CO2 through integrated modelling and data|website=Gateway to Research|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref> She has led several major NERC grants, totalling well over a £1,000,000 as principal investigator.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gotw.nerc.ac.uk/list_med_pi.asp?pi=-187650&cookieConsent=A|title=GOTW – Grants on the Web|website=gotw.nerc.ac.uk|access-date=2018-03-18}}</ref> Van de Flierdt is a member of the [[Royal Society]]'s International Exchange Committee.<ref name=":1" /> She is an editor of [[Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/geochimica-et-cosmochimica-acta/editorial-board|title=Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Editorial Board}}</ref> She has appeared on the podcast ''Forecast: Climate Conversations''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/podcast/forecast-climate-conversations-with-michael-white/id1050871256?mt=2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702051944/https://itunes.apple.com/us/podcast/forecast-climate-conversations-with-michael-white/id1050871256?mt=2|archive-date=July 2, 2017|title=Forecast: climate conversations with Michael White by Michael White on Apple Podcasts|website=Apple Podcasts|language=en|access-date=2018-03-17}}</ref>
